scenario.name: Google Threat Analysis Group (TAG), Amnesty Tech & Android Security Bulletin — Android Kernel Binder/GPU & SELinux Audit Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine a strictly walled glass playroom inside a modern smartphone where untrusted web pages are allowed to draw pictures but cannot touch the building’s master wiring. An intruder slips a rigged drawing request through the graphics pass-through slot to break the lock on the central control room, turns off the building’s master safety guardrails, and starts a silent full-privilege worker directly from memory without ever registering an app nameplate on the front lobby directory. In this scenario (T1404, Google Threat Analysis Group , TAG, Amnesty Tech & Android Security Bulletin, Android Kernel Binder/GPU & SELinux Audit Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: sandboxed isolated_app Renderer ioctl Calls, then sELinux Enforcing State, then privileged Dalvik/ART Runtime Spawn. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Sandboxed isolated_app Renderer ioctl Calls, then SELinux Enforcing State, then Privileged Dalvik/ART Runtime Spawn, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1404 across the documented kill chain.

specs.value: Apply monthly Android Security Bulletin patches promptly and restrict untrusted isolated_app SELinux domains from opening direct GPU device nodes via seccomp-bpf filters.

stages.title: Stage 1: Sandboxed isolated_app Renderer ioctl() Calls to /dev/mali0 or /dev/binder
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation (T1404 - Exploitation for Privilege Escalation)
stages.description: Trapped inside the walled glass playroom, the compromised web viewer repeatedly shoves malformed control tokens through the graphics and intercom pass-through slots until the central control room accidentally hands back a freed memory locker it is still using. A compromised Chrome renderer process running under the restricted u:r:isolated_app:s0 SELinux context invokes ioctl() system calls against /dev/mali0 (GPU driver) or /dev/binder to trigger a kernel use-after-free condition (logged in Linux Audit Event 16 with SourceSelinuxContext=u:r:isolated_app:s0 , Browser Renderer Sandbox, TargetDeviceNode=/dev/mali0 , GPU Kernel Driver, AndroidBulletinRef=CVE-2023-4211 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes adb bugreport ./android-bugreport.zip (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , adb bugreport ./android-bugreport.zip via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1404 during "Sandboxed isolated_app Renderer ioctl, Calls to /dev/mali0 or /dev/binder" , A compromised Chrome renderer process running under the restricted u:r:isolated_app:s0 SELinux context invokes ioctl, system calls against /dev/mali0 , GPU driver or /dev/binder to trigger a kernel use-after-free condition while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact mvt-android check-bugreport --output ./mvt-android-out ./android-bugreport.zip runs (which Runs Mobile Verification Toolkit , mvt-ios / mvt-android forensic parsers or inspects cellular GRX/IPX GTP-C/GTP-U roaming signaling , mvt-android so that identifies zero-click mobile spyware execution traces, kernel driver privilege escalation, or anomalous cross-carrier roaming tunnels , T1404 during "Sandboxed isolated_app Renderer ioctl, Calls to /dev/mali0 or /dev/binder"). stages.title: Stage 2: SELinux Enforcing State & Kernel task_struct Credential Overwrite Telemetry
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1562.001 - Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools / SELinux)
stages.description: Using that stolen control-room reach, the intruder erases their visitor wristband down to master superintendent zero and flips the building’s mandatory enforcement breaker from strict lock to silent permissive mode, leaving a telltale breaker-flip stamp in the engineering ring log. Using arbitrary kernel read/write primitives, the exploit zeroes out the process cred->uid/gid fields and patches selinux_state.enforcing in kernel memory, leaving diagnostic anomalies in dmesg / last_kmsg and auditd state transition logs (logged in Linux Audit Event 1404 with AuditEventType=MAC_STATUS , 1404, SelinuxTransition=old_enforcing=1 -> enforcing=0 , Runtime Kernel Patch, ForensicSource=Android bugreport kernel ring buffer so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes grep -E "avc:|selinux_state|enforcing" bugreport-dumpstate_board.txt (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , grep -E "avc:|selinux_state|enforcing" bugreport-dumpstate_board.txt via System / Runtime Ex so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1562.001 during "SELinux Enforcing State & Kernel task_struct Credential Overwrite Telemetry" , Using arbitrary kernel read/write primitives, the exploit zeroes out the process cred->uid/gid fields and patches selinux_state while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ dmesg | grep -E "selinux|avc: permissive" / ⇠#2 ACK 1404) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Binder IPC / Mali GPU Driver), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 /system/bin/app_process64).

keySpecs.value: Leverage hardware-backed Hypervisor Kernel Data Protection (KDP / RKP) to make cred structures and selinux_state read-only in physical RAM.

stages.title: Stage 3: Privileged Dalvik/ART Runtime Spawn via /system/bin/app_process64
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1623 - Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell / app_process64)
stages.description: Now holding master superintendent authority, the intruder avoids posting any visible shop sign in the phone’s main app directory and instead launches the building’s own built-in runtime engine pointing directly at a hidden blueprint stashed in a temporary closet. To execute a resident Java/DEX spyware module with root/system privileges without installing a visible APK in PackageManager, the loader spawns /system/bin/app_process64 loading a hidden DEX archive from /data/local/tmp/ or memfd (logged in Linux Audit Event 59 with HostBinary=/system/bin/app_process64, LoadedDexPath=CLASSPATH=/data/local/tmp/.cache.jar, ParentPidAnomaly=PPID=1 , init instead of zygote64 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes ps -A -o USER,PID,PPID,LABEL,NAME,ARGS | grep app_process64 (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ps -A -o USER,PID,PPID,LABEL,NAME,ARGS | grep app_process64 via System / Runtime Execution I so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1623 during "Privileged Dalvik/ART Runtime Spawn via /system/bin/app_process64" , To execute a resident Java/DEX spyware module with root/system privileges without installing a visible APK in PackageManager, the loader spawns /system/bin/app_process64 loading a hidden DEX archive from /data/local/tmp/ or memfd while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ CLASSPATH=/data/local/tmp/.cache.jar /system/bin/app_process64 /system/bin com.core.service.Main / ⇠#3 ACK 59) from Node ③ (#3 Binder IPC / Mali GPU Driver) to Node ④ (#4 Android Linux Kernel & SELinux), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 /system/bin/app_process64).
